newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran says Mideast summit doomed to fail.
newsitem.headline: Iran says Mideast summit doomed to fail.

text.p: Iranian state radio on Monday blasted a U.S. sponsored Arab-Israeli summit as an election ploy by the White House and said it was doomed to fail.

"Can a meeting whose final aims are to insure the position of the White House in upcoming elections and to suppress the new intifada (Palestinian uprising) be a solid basis for solving the acute crisis in the occupied territories?," Tehran radio said.
"Many Middle East experts believe...that this meeting is doomed to fail," added the radio in a commentary.

It was referring to the summit in Washington on Tuesday called by the United States to salvage the Middle East peace process threatened after a new cycle of Israeli-Palestinian violence last week killed nearly 70 people.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Palestinian President Yasser Arafat and King Hussein of Jordan will attend the two-day summit, the White House said. Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak declined to attend.
Iran says Israel has no right to exist and condemns the peace process as a sellout of Palestinian rights.
